concepts.statement_en: Gather the person’s concern in a comfortable setting using attentive, respectful listening and open questions.
concepts.source: presentation slides 52, 54–56; facilitator-guide PDF 28; reference-manual PDF 18–19

concepts.statement_en: Acknowledge emotion, allow time, avoid interruption and judgment, and adapt verbal and nonverbal communication.
Assess collected information: distinguish what the person reports, observations, and information still needing confirmation.
concepts.source: presentation slide 52; facilitator-guide PDF 28 learning outcome b

concepts.statement_en: Record and present relevant information clearly to the appropriate health team member.
concepts.source: presentation slide 52; facilitator-guide PDF 28 learning outcome c

concepts.statement_en: Combine open questions with focused clarification and check the meaning of a response.
Present an actionable health message and check understanding while staying within the BHW role.
concepts.source: facilitator-guide PDF 28 recommendation 4; reference-manual HEPO communication section; AHRQ Communicate Clearly / Teach-Back tools

concepts.statement_en: Apply communication skills to household profiling without collecting or sharing unnecessary personal details.
Listen to family-planning concerns and connect the person with the midwife for individual counseling.
Respond supportively to a person reporting persistent low mood and facilitate qualified help.
Explore a resident’s concerns about smoking without blame and support a practical next step.
Use the Rosario case to identify information and access barriers rather than assume poor motivation.
concepts.source: facilitator-guide PDF 28 supplementary case; kwento-ni-rosario.md provenance and case analysis
